newsitem.title: UK: Canadian bonds outstrip others in week - Salomon.
newsitem.headline: Canadian bonds outstrip others in week - Salomon.

text.p: Canadian bonds maintained their lead in the world government bond index in the week to November 7, Salomon Brothers said on Friday.

Speculation earlier in the week that the Bank of Canada might cut interest rates again, on the back of the recent strength of the Canadian dollar, coupled with buying from U.S. and overseas investors boosted Canadian bonds.
They rose 1.34 percent in local currency terms and 2.06 percent in U.S. dollar terms.
According to Salomon's the overall bond index rose 0.30 percent in local currency terms, 0.77 percent in dollars.
High yielding European bonds also faired well during the week, followed by core European government bonds and U.S. Treasuries.
Italian and Spanish government bonds were spurred on by continued positive speculation surrounding European Economic and Monetary Union and the prospect of further interest rate cuts in Italy.
Italian bonds gained 1.06 percent and Spanish bonds gained 0.95 percent in local currency terms, and 0.99 percent and 1.24 percent respectively in dollar terms.
They were followed by French governement bonds which rose by 0.55 percent in French franc terms and 0.75 percent in dollars.

U.S. Treasuries also made a respectable showing in a week which has seen the U.S. Presidential and Congressional elections and auctions of 10- and 30-year paper. They rose 0.47 percent to come in in fifth place in local currency terms.
Just behind Treasuries, German government bonds rose 0.43 percent in marks and 0.79 percent in dollar terms.
But Japanese government bonds (JGBs) and British government bonds both were losers and ended up the weakest performers of the week.
British bonds had a deficit of 0.43 percent in sterling but rose 0.69 percent in dollar terms. While JGBs showed a 0.46 percent loss in yen terms, although in dollar terms they gained 1.30 percent.

Salomon's bond index is calculated using all government bonds with over one year to maturity, weighted for market capitalisation. Only bonds freely available to institutional investors and with a certain minimum amount outstanding are included. Returns take account of price moves and accrued interest.
